Timothy,

Appreciate the clear asks — we'll get a concise packet together. High level answers up front:

- Provenance: every request is tagged with immutable metadata at ingress (tenant_id, route_id, model_version, request_id, received_at, client_cert_id). That metadata is carried end-to-end through the control plane and attached to traces and audit events.
- Storage: control-plane metadata and audit events are written to a write-once append store (WORM) for the retention period you specify. These records are partitioned by account and access-controlled via RBAC; only authorized auditors and the customer's own service accounts can query raw provenance records.
- Isolation: network and runtime isolation are enforced at three layers: per-tenant runtime containers on dedicated worker pools (or strongly-sliced multi-tenant pools by request-shard), sidecar ACLs that prevent cross-tenant KV/metadata access, and strict read-only aggregation for global metrics.

I'll loop in Monica and Vanessa to add architecture diagrams and sample audit records. We'll attach a diagram and a small evidence packet you can hand to your SOC folks before EOD Monday.

Best,
Ben

Timothy — adding the technical detail you asked for and a diagram. See inline Q&A and the attached PDF for the visual flow. Key points:

1) Ingress tagging & immutable envelope
- At the ingress gateway (customer-facing API), a Request Envelope is created. Fields: tenant_id, request_id (UUIDv4), client_cert_id (if mTLS), api_key_hash, route_id, model_version_hint. This envelope is marshaled into a signed header (HMAC-SHA256 using control-plane signing key) so downstream components can detect tampering.

2) Propagation & runtime bookkeeping
- The signed envelope is propagated via HTTP/gRPC headers to the routing layer which records the event in the request-trace. The routing layer selects a worker according to tenant policy and attaches the same request_id to all logs and KV cache operations.

3) Append-only provenance store
- Provenance events (ingress, route decision, model load, inference completion, egress) are batched and written to our append-only store (object storage with immutability flags + ledger layer). Entries are partitioned by customer account and time window; they include a hash chain to detect deletion or tampering. We can export a sample ledger slice for your auditors with redaction of other accounts.

4) Access controls and auditability
- The control plane enforces IAM checks before any raw provenance read. Customer-owned audit roles can pull exports into their own S3/GCS buckets via signed, time-limited export jobs. Internal SRE access requires dual-approval and is logged.

5) Cross-region/fallback scenarios
- When routing falls back (region/variant), we replicate minimal runbook metadata (request_id, original_region, fallback_reason) — full provenance remains available in the original account partition. Cross-region replication uses encrypted, account-scoped topics; critical evidence retains a pointer to the canonical ledger entry to avoid duplication that could leak tenant mappings.

Sample log snippets are in the attached PDF (redwood-control-plane-dataflow.pdf) showing JSON event types and field names. Let us know if you want a short sandbox export.

Regards,

Timothy — a few notes focused on network and runtime isolation that often end up as procurement checklist items:

- Network tenancy: control-plane components (control API, orchestration, scheduler) live in a distinct management VPC. Customer inference traffic traverses isolated customer subnets; we provide VPC peering or private-link style connectors for Private deployments so control-plane metadata never traverses the public internet.

- Sidecar enforcement: each worker runs a lightweight sidecar that enforces KV and metadata ACLs. Sidecars reject any requests where request_id tenant_id mismatch is detected. Sidecar-to-sidecar communication uses mTLS with per-tenant SVIDs (SPIFFE-compatible) so mutual identity is verified at the transport layer.

- Telemetry sampling & redaction: by default we sample verbose payloads for internal telemetry at 0.1% and store payload hashes instead of raw text. For customers that require full-fidelity audit logs, we provide an opt-in export pipeline that writes raw payloads directly into the customer's own bucket under their control.

- Mitigation of reconstruction risk: we avoid storing cross-tenant correlation keys in any shared index. Global metrics are aggregated from account-scoped counters; any cross-account joins require explicit, auditable jobs run with restricted service identities.

If your compliance team wants, Neha can provide a short note on how these controls satisfy specific SOC/ISO controls.

-Vanessa
